Jane Example Founder & CEO · 3rd+ 3h

I used to think productivity was about doing more. I was wrong. After years of optimizing every single hour of my day, I finally realized that the highest-leverage move is subtraction, not addition. Here is what actually changed for me. First, I stopped measuring my output in hours and started measuring it in outcomes that mattered to customers. Second, I cut every recurring meeting that did not have a clear decision attached to it, and the calendar suddenly had room to breathe. Third, I built a single source of truth for priorities so my team never had to guess what mattered most this week. The results genuinely surprised me. We shipped faster than before, the team felt noticeably calmer, and our customers noticed the difference almost immediately. The lesson is simple to say but hard to live by: clarity beats intensity, and less truly is more when every remaining thing is the right thing. What is one commitment you could remove this week to make room for the work that actually moves the needle?
